pr_title: Exit the lock before we call into user code and handle losing the race for the RCW table
pr_comments: Tests for this specific deadlock are still TODO, but I've reorganized the code for the NativeAOT ComWrappers implementation to match the same order of logic as the CoreCLR implementation and encapsulated each step into separate helper functions (which also helped significantly clarify lock usage).
Validated that the ComWrappers tests pass locally and added a test for the deadlock. This is ready for review!
@jkoritzinsky Can you please run GCStress locally? Ideally we'd also include some amount of JITStress too. I'm also fine kicking off the legs that run too.
Do we have GCStress support for NativeAOT?
@jkoritzinsky Oh, right. I think we do, but we don't have a CI for it. @MichalStrehovsky Do we have a way to run GCStress on local native AOT?
There is no GC stress for native AOT.
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 1 pipeline(s).

Not exactly the same (although @EgorBo said it's kinda close enough? 😅), I've added an option in the Microsoft Store to simulate GC stress (I basically just spawn a thread that just spams `GC.Collect(); Thread.Wait(50);` in a loop). Perhaps it'd help if I also tested with that mode enabled for a bit, just to double check things don't blow up when that's running?
NativeAOT outerloop failures are unrelated. Can I get one more review pass?

I tested with the Microsoft Store and everything seems to work fine:

- Checked out `release/9.0-staging` (f58036422045bc89fa2e70536be5a857614cfee8)
- Cherry-pick https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/110551
- Cherry-pick https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/110685
- Cherry-pick https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/110828
- Cherry-pick https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/110762
  - Branch with all changes: https://github.com/Sergio0694/runtime/commits/user/sergiopedri/store-testing/
- Build with `.\build.cmd clr.aot -c Release`
- Set `IlcSdkPath` in the Store .csproj to `runtime\artifacts\bin\coreclr\windows.x64.Release\aotsdk\`
- Set `GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild`
- Switch to Release
- Deploy

I used the Store for a while, including closing and launching it a few times, with and without our "GC stress" mode enabled as well (which creates a thread that just spams `GC.Collect()` every 50 milliseconds in a loop). Couldn't find any issues 🎉

Could we backport this one too? I _think_ it should be our last blocker from the NAOT side for shipping 😄
Thank you!

combase.dll!CStdIdentity::CInternalUnk::QueryInterface(const _GUID & riid, void * * ppv) Line 428 C++ .exe!S_P_CoreLib_System_Runtime_InteropServices_ComWrappers_NativeObjectWrapper__Create() Line 514 Unknown > .exe!S_P_CoreLib_System_Runtime_InteropServices_ComWrappers__TryGetOrCreateObjectForComInstanceInternal() Line 1064 Unknown .exe!S_P_CoreLib_System_Runtime_InteropServices_ComWrappers__GetOrCreateObjectForComInstance() Line 799 Unknown .exe!WinRT_Runtime_WinRT_ComWrappersSupport__CreateRcwForComObject_0() Unknown .exe!WinRT_Runtime_WinRT_MarshalInspectable_1__FromAbi() Unknown .exe!Microsoft_Windows_SDK_NET_WinRT_GenericTypeInstantiations_Windows_Foundation_AsyncOperationCompletedHandler_1_Windows_Graphics_Imaging_PixelDataProvider__Do_Abi_Invoke() Unknown ```
Dump shared internally, opening this just for tracking (same as #110747). From @MichalStrehovsky: > "This thing [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8edcc3123615dfe02fbd830505b2acdd5f428bfa/src/coreclr/nativeaot/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/ComWrappers.NativeAot.cs#L1044-L1078) acquires a lock and then `NativeObjectWrapper.Create` goes on to call `QueryInterface` on who-knows-what that acquires some lock. We then have several threads waiting for this global `ComWrappers._lock` lock that is never released because we’re blocked inside the `QueryInterface`. CoreCLR uses a different locking strategy and `NativeObjectWrapper.Create` doesn’t seem to be running under a lock from what I see."

review_comments: Is the issue here thread affinity or COM apartment affinity?

I believe the original deadlock was due to COM apartment affinity with the STA vs a Free-threaded apartment thread.

In any case, this test ensures that we're able to create an RCW while we're in the middle of creating an RCW on another thread, which was what was occurring in the original issue.

My concern here is we've no idea the apartment state in this case. If the apartment state is relevant, then we could be accidentially testing the wrong thing. If this is indeed an STA related issue, then we should create an STA thread and test that as such.

This isn't wrong, just potentially breeding confidence in having more testing coverage than we do.
I've added a test that explicitly marshals a COM object across apartments and hits the right code-paths.

I agree that moving the RCW cache logic into this separate type helps with maintainability, but I'm wondering if we could make this a `struct` (and make the `_rcwCache` field not readonly) to avoid an extra indirection every time we need to use it, which is pretty often? We don't really need this to be a class anyway, it's only ever used internally in this file, and it doesn't have a finalizer or anything. Thoughts? 🙂
It makes little sense to turn this into a `struct`. Every method here takes a lock. The indirection is noise in most cases and the lock means it won't even be measurable in practice.

Should we add a comment to this field and the one below to also mention the fact that "Native object wrapper = RCW" and "Managed object wrapper = CCW"? The acronyms are widely used, and I feel like if we just rename the fields and drop all references to them, other readers might get confused 🤔
Yes, this also acts as a null check.
